intake.original:
## Destination

A buildable spec for Hemiciclo v1, ready for `to-spec` and `to-tickets`: a Country Dashboard the owner checks daily plus an Article Lens for pasted articles, both held to the Narration rules, with content produced by agent runs on the owner's account rather than by in-app model calls.

## Notes

- **Domain.** A neutral, at-a-glance view of each country's political situation. "Hemiciclo" is a code name, not the brand. Every session reads `CONTEXT.md` for the vocabulary and calls the `grilling` and `domain-modeling` skills unless a ticket says otherwise.
- **Neutrality is the product.** Present what happened, never why it was good or bad. The four **Narration rules**, settled while charting:
  1. Events read as actor → action → stated aim, and the aim is attributed to the actor.
  2. No causal or adversative connective in Hemiciclo's own voice (*so, because, therefore, but, despite, in response to*). A causal link appears only as an attributed claim.
  3. A law or programme is described by what it does mechanically, not by what it intends. Its official name is marked as a name and never reused as a description.
  4. Numbers, not intensifiers: no *massive, sweeping* or *controversial*. Give figures, and both parties' estimates where they differ.
- **Lexicon.** A product glossary, distinct from the repo's `CONTEXT.md`. It holds a controlled vocabulary of forms of government and reserved words, each marked *defined*, *quote-only* or *banned*. The default form of government is the constitutional one. Third-party assessments such as V-Dem appear only attributed, if at all in v1. A small seed ships in v1.
- **Country Brief.** Fixed sections: who governs, how they got there, what's next, and the top live issues with sources. Hard facts come from structured sources, and only the live-issue prose is model-written. Every claim links its source, and each Brief shows the model and the generation time. No "temperature" signal in v1.
- **Generation.** The app never calls a writing model. Visiting a country without a Brief shows "We're still gathering data for this country, check back later" and records a **Generation Request**. During the soak test, only the owner's requests are honoured. A headless Claude Code job on the owner's account, run on a timer on the homelab Pi ([runtime findings](https://github.com/lutzseverino/hemiciclo/issues/13)), works through requests, refreshes followed countries daily, and posts Brief bundles through a protected ingest endpoint. Bundles follow a fixed schema so an API-backed Generator can replace the job later. Hemiciclo flags stale Briefs itself, since no runtime reports whether a Brief was actually produced and ingested. The app never stores the owner's Claude login. The Jev API key is a server-side secret of `services/hemiciclo`, never exposed to the browser. Mock fixtures cover the soak-test countries.
- **Article Lens v1.** Jev classifies in-app and synchronously, through the owner's Jev API access. The overview arrives asynchronously through the generation queue. No chat in v1.
- **Classifier.** Framing signals first: article type (news, opinion or analysis), attribution ratio, Lexicon-flagged loaded terms, one-sided sourcing and emotional intensity. Leaning signals come second, multi-axis and relative to each country's own spectrum, shown with confidence. Outlet ratings are aggregated from Hemiciclo's own article labels, and third-party ratings serve only as private calibration.
- **Storage** ([storage findings](https://github.com/lutzseverino/hemiciclo/issues/6)). Store URL, outlet, date, byline, headline, labels, Hemiciclo's own fact-based summary (never a close paraphrase or translation), and a publisher excerpt of at most 200 characters. Full text from feeds, fetched pages or pasted articles is processed in memory and never stored. Ingest drops feed `content:encoded` and cuts `description` to the excerpt cap. Jev receives only the text a question needs, because TypeSafe may retain submitted text (MCA §4.1(c)).
- **Shape.** A pnpm workspace modelled on lutzseverino/polity: `apps/web`, `packages/design`, `packages/ui`, `services/hemiciclo` (Spring Boot consuming Cardo from Maven Central) and `deploy/`. Cardo is used unchanged. The soak test runs on the owner's homelab behind Cardo/Keycloak login.
- **Soak-test countries:** Spain, United States, Argentina and India.
- **Language:** English for v1, with an internationalisation-ready UI. Sources stay in their original language.

## Decisions so far

- [Establish whether owner-account agent runs may produce Hemiciclo content](https://github.com/lutzseverino/hemiciclo/issues/5): yes for the soak test, through unmodified Claude Code with the app never holding the credential. A public site, or serving anyone else's requests, needs API billing, a human review gate and AI disclosure. ([findings](https://github.com/lutzseverino/hemiciclo/blob/research/subscription-generation-terms/docs/development/research/subscription-generation-terms.md))
- [Establish what Jev's API offers for classification and checking](https://github.com/lutzseverino/hemiciclo/issues/4): one endpoint, with one text and many Choice/Score/Noul questions per request, at $0.042 per million input tokens, a 64k context and about 110 ms per call. First-option bias is countered by sending every rotation of a Choice and marking disagreement as uncertain. No Java SDK. Labels are ours to show, with an AI disclosure. ([findings](https://github.com/lutzseverino/hemiciclo/blob/research/jev-api/docs/development/research/jev-api.md))
- [Find free sources of structured political metadata for every country](https://github.com/lutzseverino/hemiciclo/issues/3): Wikidata (CC0, live) for who holds office, IPU Parline (keyless, CC BY-NC-SA) for legislative elections, the next expected vote and the political system, and Constitute to cite constitutions. ElectionGuide is optional for presidential votes. ParlGov is out. ([findings](https://github.com/lutzseverino/hemiciclo/blob/research/political-metadata-sources/docs/development/research/political-metadata-sources.md))
- [Choose the runtime for the soak-test Generator](https://github.com/lutzseverino/hemiciclo/issues/13): a headless `claude -p` job on the always-on Pi, started by a systemd timer and signed in with a `claude setup-token` token. It's first-party, reaches the ingest endpoint privately over the homelab network, and drops T3's grey zone. Routines can't reach the homelab without a public endpoint, and Desktop tasks skip runs while the computer sleeps. ([findings](https://github.com/lutzseverino/hemiciclo/blob/research/generator-runtime/docs/development/research/generator-runtime.md))
- [Find free sources of political news for the soak-test countries](https://github.com/lutzseverino/hemiciclo/issues/2): GDELT's raw 15-minute files for discovery in all four countries (commercial reuse with attribution, no excerpts; its search API is too throttled). Outlets' own RSS feeds add excerpts during the personal soak test only, since their terms are personal and non-commercial. Wikipedia Current events is only a thin, CC BY-SA cross-check. ([findings](https://github.com/lutzseverino/hemiciclo/blob/research/political-news-sources/docs/development/research/political-news-sources.md))
- [Establish what Hemiciclo may store and show from news articles](https://github.com/lutzseverino/hemiciclo/issues/6): store metadata, labels, Hemiciclo's own fact-based summary and a publisher excerpt of at most 200 characters. Full text is processed in memory only and never stored. The owner-only soak test falls under private-use exceptions. Spain is the tightest constraint for any public excerpt. ([findings](https://github.com/lutzseverino/hemiciclo/blob/research/article-storage-rights/docs/development/research/article-storage-rights.md))

## Not yet specified

- How Hemiciclo deploys and authenticates on the homelab, once the workspace and pipeline shape are settled, including where the ingest endpoint lives: on the homeserver, which the Pi job would wake first, or on the Pi.
- Where the Generator's instructions live. Keeping them in this repository as skills would let an API-key Generator reuse them unchanged.
- Following countries: what "followed" means, and how it drives daily refresh.
- Article Lens flow: how a pasted article enters, and how its asynchronous overview reaches the owner.
- How outlet ratings aggregate from article labels, once the Jev test-run shows label quality.
- A neutrality regression set: how Brief wording is checked over time against the Narration rules.
- Whether and how attributed third-party regime assessments appear.
- When Spanish localisation lands.

## Out of scope

- The paid tier: in-app chat, one-click research and fact-checking, and subscriptions. This includes the likely Cardo enhancement for metered AI usage on Billing entitlements.
- Community calibration votes ("this feels left-leaning").
- Training Hemiciclo's own classifier on Jev's labels: the MCA bans training a model that imitates Jev's output (§2.3(b), per [the Jev findings](https://github.com/lutzseverino/hemiciclo/issues/4)). Aggregating labels into Outlet ratings is unaffected.
- The public brand name and the public launch. Per [the terms findings](https://github.com/lutzseverino/hemiciclo/issues/5), a launch needs API-billed generation, a human review gate before publication, and AI disclosure. Naming Jev or TypeSafe on public labels needs their permission (MCA §16.4). IPU Parline, Constitute and ElectionGuide data are licensed for non-commercial use only, and Parline's ShareAlike term may reach Briefs that republish it ([metadata findings](https://github.com/lutzseverino/hemiciclo/issues/3)). A launch also needs a per-outlet rights registry (text-and-data-mining opt-outs and RSS terms decide whether full text may reach Jev), an answer from TypeSafe on retention or zero data retention, and a lawyer's review of the open points in the storage findings. Outlet RSS terms are mostly personal and non-commercial, and Spain's art. 129 bis likely requires publisher permission for public excerpts, so a launch shows headline and link only unless excerpts are licensed ([news findings](https://github.com/lutzseverino/hemiciclo/issues/2)).
- Mobile and landing apps.
